finding: All tested variants preserve the analytical nonlinear iteration and backtracking path in all six previously failing cases.
Wet-regime response error is strongly reduced by tighter conductivity accuracy; tightening retention alone has little or no effect in B01-wet, B12-wet and O05-wet.
Dry-regime errors improve when knot density increases, but the shared support means the theta-versus-K attribution is not clean because a tighter K criterion also improves retention interpolation.
important_caveat: Because theta/C and K currently share knot locations, tightening one component can improve the other component indirectly. F-AHL11 therefore identifies regime sensitivity but does not provide fully orthogonal component attribution in dry cases.
next_action: Prospectively test 1e-3 retention and/or logK accuracy on the frozen six cases. If those gates still fail, redesign the error metric rather than continuing arbitrary global densification.
nonclaims: No F-AHL10 response gate is relaxed.
No performance or production claim follows from this attribution.
